## Pull request overview

This PR removes reserve-sponsorship behavior from XChainBridge-related transaction processing, simplifying reserve checks and owner-count adjustments so they no longer consider a transaction-provided sponsor.

- Simplified `applyCreateAccountAttestations` by removing the `STTx` parameter and related sponsorship logic.

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: `finalizeClaimHelper` now decrements owner counts via `adjustOwnerCount(..., {}, -1, ...)` after erasing the ClaimID SLE. That bypasses the existing `adjustOwnerCountObj` logic, which correctly accounts for a possibly-sponsored ledger object (sfSponsor) when updating `sfSponsoredOwnerCount`/`sfSponsoringOwnerCount`. Even if new XChain txs no longer create sponsored objects, previously-created (or otherwise sponsored) ClaimID entries would be deleted incorrectly and can trip the sponsorship invariants.

## High Level Overview of Change

This pull request introduces the functionality needed to support bridging assets across ledgers. This implementation focus on connecting two XRPL-like ledgers. > Potentially the actual problem is that the door should be paying the SignatureReward for the XChainClaim

Well, we want the amounts locked on the door in the locking chain to match the amounts issued by the door on the issuing chain. reviewCommentsList.body:
It looks like this code is intended to allow an attestor to sign an attestation using the Door account's master or RegularKey.  It that's what is happening I don't think that's a good idea.

The attestations are modeled after commonly used multisignatures in the XRPLedger.  You can't use the master key or regular key of the signed-for account if you use multisignatures.  You can _only_ use the multisigners in the `SignerList` owned by the account.

My strong recommendation would be to remove the code that allows a master or regular key to be used in this way.

I'm afraid that this change was the result of misunderstanding a comment I made earlier: https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/pull/4292#i

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
This `!amt.native()` check allows a simple transfer of sufficient XRP (not an account creation) to create an account.  This gives XChain transfers two distinct ways to create an account:

1. With a regular claimID and cross-chain transfer of sufficient XRP.
2. With an `XChainAccountCreateCommit` transaction.

I feel like having two very different ways to achieve the same end complicates things for documentation and for users.

reviewCommentsList.author: mvadari
reviewCommentsList.body:
This is also a feature because I requested it - it's a lot easier to bootstrap a bridge when you don't need to create a temporary multisign in order to set up the initial accounts (e.g. the witness submission accounts). 

I believe the reason it was believed to be fine to do it this way is because the threat model is the same regardless - you need to trust whoever controls the account, whether that is via owning the master key/regular key or via a quorum of multisigners, since they could theoretically sign any transaction to mishandle those funds. Also, any properly set up bridge should disable the master key and should not have a regular key enabled.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Given that we're talking about a side chain, precautions like insisting on a specific issuing account or a minimum amount of XRP in that account end up only being guidelines.  Side chains don't run the same code as the main chain.

1. It would be easy for a side chain to have a different genesis account.
2. It would be easy for a side chain to have a different starting amount of XRP.

While that's true, I don't have a strong opinion about whether any of these guidelines are retained/used.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
@mvadari, I can see how that feature add would be a convenience in certain testing scenarios.

Part of what I'm driving toward is to keep the rules and behavior for attestation handling as similar as possible to multisigning of XRPL transactions, since attestations model multisigning.  I think maintaining this kind of consistency helps users, developers, and doc folks.

>  it's a lot easier to bootstrap a bridge when you don't need to create a temporary multisign in order to set up the initial accounts

Really?  A _lot_ easier?  Setting up multisigning requires a single transaction, two transactions if you also disable the master key.  And you have to do that once for each of the two chains.
